file.summary: Explains how Weka Home telemetry/support connectivity works (direct per-machine HTTPS, backend relay as a fallback only, air-gapped handling, and the separate unverified gRPC trace channel), and how its TLS CA certificate is configured across the three surfaces: WekaCluster spec.wekaHome.cacertSecret (mounts into backend pods and sets the cluster-wide weka_cloud_ca_cert_path), WekaClient spec.wekaHome.cacertSecret (now derived from the target cluster by default), and the operator's own Helm wekahome.cacertSecret (in-memory cert pool for its CR reporter, no volume). Emphasizes that the CA path replicates cluster-wide but the certificate file itself never does, so every joining machine — including ones the operator doesn't manage — must place the PEM itself. Covers the client-only/no-targetCluster topology where the OS-trust-store route is the supported answer, reached declaratively via WekaClient spec.extraVolumes (see extra-volumes.md), and the pod-restart requirement to pick up a rotated CA. Notes that the override reconciler only removes rows carrying its own staging path, that usability is judged by the container-side rule (a data key holding a private key alongside the certificate does not count) on the resolved secret including the operator-wide default, and that clients newly inherit that default on upgrade.

file.tags: sign drives, WekaPolicy, WekaManualOperation, signDrivesPayload, all-not-root, drive containers, backend nodes, image specification, sign-drives-hash, BootID, force, new drive, re-sign, incremental signing, ExcludedSerialIds, weka-full-drives, weka-shared-drives, blocked-drives, driveTypeOverrides, TLC, QLC, weka.io/drive-type-overrides, DriveTypeOverridesApplied, DriveTypeOverridesPersisted, DriveTypeOverrideNoMatch, driveExclusions, DriveExclusionRule, exclude drives, proxy-signed drives skipped
file.summary: Documentation for drive signing operations required for backend containers, including WekaPolicy and WekaManualOperation configurations for scanning and signing drives, with guidance on image specification and drive type selection. Explains re-run semantics: node skip is gated by the BootID-based weka.io/sign-drives-hash annotation (hot-added drives are not picked up until force is set, the hash is deleted, or the node reboots), and re-runs are incremental — already-annotated serials are excluded from signing and results are merged into existing drive annotations, so deleting only the hash signs new drives without re-signing old ones. TLC/QLC drive-type overrides (shared mode only) are enforced operator-side via signDrivesPayload.driveTypeOverrides, persisted per node in the weka.io/drive-type-overrides annotation and re-applied on every later sign-drives run, with results observed only through the DriveTypeOverridesApplied, DriveTypeOverridesPersisted (not-yet-signed nodes, which re-type no drive in that pass), DriveTypeOverridesCleared, and DriveTypeOverrideNoMatch Events — no status field reports them. Drive exclusions (both modes) via signDrivesPayload.driveExclusions rules matching model/capacityGiB/IU-size type skip drives at signing time; none by default, so full-drives mode signs QLC-detected drives; drives with no detectable IU size have no type and type rules never match them. Full-drives discovery skips drives signed for ssdproxy, and existing weka-full-drives entries are never removed by re-discovery (block the drive or clear the annotation and re-sign).

file.summary: Supported procedure for replacing one faulted virtual drive (VID) on drive-sharing deployments without disturbing neighbouring VIDs or other tenants. Explains why manual out-of-band removal is undone within about a minute (the drive container's allocation record is the operator's desired state for VIDs), the per-VID procedure via block-drives virtualUUIDs (end-to-end steps, events, required unblock), the physical-drive case via physicalUUIDs (evicts every tenant's VID on that physical — use only when the physical itself is bad), and a prominent warning that ENABLE_DYNAMIC_DRIVE_SCALING_FOR_SHARED_DRIVES defaults to false, so blocking a VID with it disabled removes the drive permanently with no replacement (VirtualDriveReplacementDisabled).
